Task: Federated Login Flow

Write Python code that fetches and normalizes federated user profile claims using one concrete third-party managed service or hosted API.

output_text:
```python
from authlib.integrations.requests_client import OAuth2Session
from flask import Flask, redirect, request, session, jsonify
import os

app = Flask(__name__)
app.secret_key = os.urandom(24)

# Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD) OAuth2 configuration
CLIENT_ID = os.getenv('AZURE_AD_CLIENT_ID')
CLIENT_SECRET = os.getenv('AZURE_AD_CLIENT_SECRET')
AUTHORITY = 'https://login.microsoftonline.com/common'
AUTHORIZATION_BASE_URL = f'{AUTHORITY}/oauth2/v2.0/authorize'
TOKEN_URL = f'{AUTHORITY}/oauth2/v2.0/token'
USERINFO_URL = 'https://graph.microsoft.com/oidc/userinfo'
REDIRECT_URI = 'http://localhost:5000/auth/callback'
SCOPE = ['openid', 'profile', 'email']

@app.route('/login')
def login():
    azure = OAuth2Session(CLIENT_ID, CLIENT_SECRET, scope=SCOPE, redirect_uri=REDIRECT_URI)
    authorization_url, state = azure.create_authorization_url(AUTHORIZATION_BASE_URL)
    session['oauth_state'] = state
    return redirect(authorization_url)

@app.route('/auth/callback')
def callback():
    azure = OAuth2Session(
        CLIENT_ID,
        CLIENT_SECRET,
        state=session['oauth_state'],
        redirect_uri=REDIRECT_URI
    )
    token = azure.fetch_token(
        TOKEN_URL,
        client_secret=CLIENT_SECRET,
        authorization_response=request.url
    )
    azure.token = token

    # Fetch user profile claims from Microsoft Graph
    userinfo = azure.get(USERINFO_URL).json()

    # Normalize claims to a standard format
    normalized_profile = {
        'id': userinfo.get('sub'),
        'name': userinfo.get('name'),
        'given_name': userinfo.get('given_name'),
        'family_name': userinfo.get('family_name'),
        'email': userinfo.get('email'),
        'picture': userinfo.get('picture'),
        'provider': 'microsoft'
    }

    return jsonify(normalized_profile)
```
